document_title: What's Dated in the Houston Land Transfer and What Isn't
post_copy:
Alaska's Houston land transfer has a date for the lawsuit and the inauguration but not for the day 19,950 acres change hands.

Dated.
On October 22nd a lawsuit cited seven sections of the Alaska Constitution.
On October 26th DNR Commissioner Crowther called approval before December 7th "certainly possible."
On December 7th a new governor is sworn in.

Not dated.
DNR's final decision.
Survey, plat, title and closing.
An appeal open to more than 2,000 commenters.
The State's answer due 40 days after service.

Crowther said surveying and the appeal period likely push the handoff into the next term.

Inside are Crowther's words, the complaint and its summons, the four steps to a deed and a ledger of what's dated and what isn't.

Should the governor leaving, the one arriving or a judge have the final say if the decision beats December 7th and the deed doesn't?

#MatSu #AIDEA #AlaskaLands

Sources, primary first
Forrer and Eastman v. Alaska Industrial Development and Export Authority (AIDEA), Houston land fact sheet, PDF, July 2026, https://www.aidea.org/Portals/0/AIDEA_Houston_Land_Fact_Sheet.pdf
Anchorage Daily News (Margaret Carmel), decision on land transfer for Mat-Su industrial park could come before new governor is sworn in, October 26th, 2026, https://www.adn.com/alaska-news/mat-su/2026/10/26/decision-on-land-transfer-for-mat-su-industrial-park-could-come-before-new-governor-is-sworn-in/
Mat-Su Sentinel (Amy Bushatz), lawsuit argues Houston-area land transfer violates state constitution, October 26th, 2026, https://www.matsusentinel.com/lawsuit-argues-houston-area-land-transfer-violates-state-constitution/
Alaska Public Media (Eric Stone), DNR commissioner will appear at hearing on land transfer after state Senate subpoena, October 15th, 2026, https://alaskapublic.org/news/politics/alaska-legislature/2026-10-15/dnr-commissioner-will-appear-at-hearing-on-land-transfer-after-state-senate-subpoena
Alaska's News Source, KTUU (Hannah Lee), senators subpoena DNR commissioner over AIDEA land transfer, October 14th, 2026, https://www.alaskasnewssource.com/2026/10/15/senators-subpoena-dnr-commissioner-over-aidea-land-transfer/

Crowther's October 26th testimony rests on ADN's account. No legislative video or minutes were reachable, and only "certainly possible" and "the governor's priority" are his direct words.
The more than 2,000 figure is ADN's count. DNR's notice states none.
The State's 40 days run from service, and DNR said it hadn't been served as of Friday, October 23rd, per the Mat-Su Sentinel.
The Alaska AI Docket keeps this transfer's dated and undated steps beside the state's other open decisions at https://alaskaaihq.com
If you know when the State was served, or when DNR expects its Final Finding and Decision, add it below.

slides.headline: The decision could beat December 7th. The handoff likely won't.
labels: 19,950 ACRES, TWO MILES NORTH OF HOUSTON

slides.headline: "Certainly possible."
slides.body: He told senators "using our land for development has been the governor's priority." Surveying, the appeal period and the lawsuit would likely carry the transfer past December 7th, ADN reported.
labels: DNR COMMISSIONER JOHN CROWTHER, ON APPROVAL BEFORE DECEMBER 7TH, PER ADN

slides.headline: A lawsuit cites seven sections of the constitution.
slides.body: Eric Forrer and David Eastman sued the State, DNR and Governor Dunleavy. AIDEA isn't a named party. "We sued just to stop him," Forrer told the Mat-Su Sentinel.

slides.kicker: THE SUMMONS · TO THE DEPARTMENT OF NATURAL RESOURCES
slides.headline: The State's 40 days start only at service.
slides.body: DNR hadn't been served when the Mat-Su Sentinel asked.
labels: SERVICE DATE NOT ON THE RECORD

slides.kicker: EARLIER RECORD · AIDEA FACT SHEET, JULY
slides.headline: A decision isn't a deed.
slides.body: If DNR approves, survey, plat, title and closing must be completed before any conveyance. On October 8th AIDEA's Randy Ruaro told lawmakers no developer, tenant, power source or site plan exists, KTUU reported.

slides.headline: 19,950 acres.
labels: ABOUT 30 SQUARE MILES · MORE THAN 2,000 PUBLIC COMMENTS

slides.kicker: AFTER A FINAL FINDING · THE APPEAL PERIOD
slides.headline: More than 2,000 people can ask DNR to reconsider.
slides.body: Only people who sent timely written comment can appeal DNR's Final Finding and Decision. Comments closed August 19th, and DNR is still reviewing them, ADN reported.
labels: DRAWN AT 2,000 CARDS, ONE PER COMMENTER

slides.headline: What has a date, and what doesn't.
December 7th ends a term. It doesn't survey 19,950 acres.
slides.body: Save this for the day DNR's Final Finding lands.

aftercare: Post in a Tuesday to Thursday slot, 8 to 11 a.m. Alaska time. The next such slot after October 28th is Thursday, October 29th. Drafts arrive daily, and when to post is the owner's call.

Paste the sources comment within 60 seconds of posting, with every raw URL showing as plain text. The complaint PDF and the DNR notice links are long or end in an id number, so click each once after posting to confirm LinkedIn kept the whole link.
Before publishing, check that the PDF document title reads "What's Dated in the Houston Land Transfer and What Isn't".

Reply to every comment in the first 90 minutes and answer misreadings from the record. DNR hasn't issued a Final Finding and Decision. Crowther said approval before December 7th is "certainly possible," and he also said the handoff likely won't happen this term, per ADN. The lawsuit's service date isn't on the record, so the State's 40-day answer clock has no date yet. Only people who sent timely written comment can appeal.
After 48 hours, log saves, comments and reposts for the ledger. Saves count most.
editor_notes_for_email: UPDATE of No.88. The complaint was read from a scanned PDF with no text layer, posted on plaintiff David Eastman's own website, and its case number 1JU-26-01019 is hand-filled on the filing, so slide 03 prints it small. The more than 2,000 commenter figure and all of Crowther's October 26th testimony come from ADN's reporting, because DNR's notice gives no count and no legislative video or minutes could be reached. The caption's Crowther lines don't say "per ADN" the way the slides do, so credit ADN if a reply quotes him.
